text:
Carmen: quick-check — we need a small decision: how do we want to present the paged+streaming API across Python/TS/Go? goal: single mental model for retries and backpressure, ergonomic for each lang. thoughts?
Alice: +1 on single mental model. my gut: surface two primitives — sync/async page iterators and a streaming callback for hot paths. keep the transport layer responsible for retries.
Ben: curious — what does "streaming callback" mean exactly? is it the same as TS async generator or more like a push handler?
Carmen: good Q. think of two common patterns: pull-mode (client iterates pages or items) and push-mode (runtime calls your handler as items arrive). need both.
Drew: For ergonomics: Python wants sync iterator and async iterator. TS uses async generator. Go uses channel-like iterator (receive-only chan). Implementations should map cleanly. also need clear retry boundaries: per-page retry vs per-item retry.
Alice: agree. propose these surface-level rules: 1) retries are bounded to idempotent page fetches — server must ensure stable page tokens. 2) streaming callback should only get items that are final (no half-retries). 3) client libs expose knobs: max_page_retries, per_request_timeout, prefetch_pages.
Ben: transport concerns: if we retry page N, do we re-send every item or use resume token? resume tokens are great but brittle. maybe prefer server-supplied page_token+offset? otherwise we'd need dedupe at app layer.
Drew: example mapping:
```python
# python sync iterator
for item in client.list_items(request):
    handle(item)

# python async iterator
async for item in client.list_items_async(request):
    await handle(item)
```
and TS:
```ts
for await (const item of client.listItems(req)) {
  await handle(item);
}
```
Go: receive on channel.
Carmen: +1 on those ergonomics. Also want to avoid surprising memory growth with prefetch. default prefetch=1, opt-in for higher.
Alice: backlog/backpressure: transport should expose a window size to runtime. e.g., grpc stream credits or http/2 flow control. client libs translate to internal prefetch limit.
Ben: semantics for errors mid-stream: prefer this policy: transient network -> retry page fetch up to max_page_retries; permanent -> raise and surface last-good-resume-token. For push-mode, call on_error hook then stop.
Drew: Minor note: file a tiny RFC for token shape: page_token + item_offset (int). simpler than opaque resume blobs and easier to reason about idempotency.
Carmen: can someone prototype how we surface max_page_retries default and override in each lang? Ideally config object on client construction and per-call override.
Alice: I'll sketch in the python/ts/go SDK apis:
- python: Client(..., pagination_config=PaginationConfig(prefetch=1, max_page_retries=2))
- ts: new Client({ pagination: { prefetch:1, maxPageRetries:2 } })
- go: client := NewClient(WithPagination(Pagination{Prefetch:1, MaxPageRetries:2}))

infra-bot: RFC link: https://go.redwood/repo/paging-handshake — PR opened for token-shape proposal (draft).
Ben: one more thing: we should document migration story if server changes token format. add compatibility header e.g., X-Page-Token-Version.
Carmen: solid. next step: Alice to draft API stubs + short compatibility RFC. Drew will sketch token shape PR. Ben/infra-bot will review transport implications for grpc/http. Thanks :thumbsup:
